still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.

Congress has not passed a permanent Medicare obesity benefit, and the statutory Part D exclusion of weight-loss drugs is still in law. Medicare's new obesity reach runs only through a CMMI demonstration and the existing diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind.
DOT's 2033 interpretive guidance still treats prescribed, disclosed incretins as non-disqualifying for commercial drivers, including AUD and off-label calm use.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 42.5% ever-used − 31.6% current = 10.9% of adults who used and are off now. ~44% of current users are on a second or later course (13.9 points; the share held near 45% because ~5 points of first-time users, mostly Medicare-model and Medicaid starters, offset ~2.5M involuntary stops during the 2035 Wegovy-pill shortage, about half of whom restarted). 3.4 points cycled and are off again, so (13.9 + 3.4) / 42.5 ≈ 40.7%. The other 7.5 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, and restart within a year of 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×17.5 + 0.33×31 + 0.24×42 + 0.23×34 = 3.5 + 10.2 + 10.1 + 7.8 ≈ 31.6. Income thirds average 31.5. Users: 31.6% of ~276M adults ≈ 87.2M, up ~10.5M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial 15.0M (17%); Medicare 19.6M (22%; 14.0M on existing codes + 5.6M in the Metabolic Access Model); Medicaid 7.5M (9%); free public provision 1.0M (HRSA settlement supply 0.75M + NY/CA/IL state programmes 0.25M); legitimate cash 30.5M (35%); imported/counterfeit 13.6M (16%, down from 15.4M). Sum 87.2M. Publicly paid or provided = 28.1M (32%), so public programmes together are now the largest payer of incretin fills. Cash breaks down as 11.0M weight, 12.0M longevity/'metabolic health', 4.6M calm/focus, 1.9M Reset and 1.0M AUD = 30.5M. ~19M current users (22%) have a BMI under 30, and ~6.5M are under 25. Adult obesity is ~31.0%. ~16% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, down from 19%, still concentrated in non-opt-in Southern states and among the uninsured working poor above Medicaid limits. Pediatric: 1.4% of under-18s, with 12–17s at ~3.0% and 6–11s at ~0.3% after the Nov 2035 semaglutide approval. Under-12 weight prescribing stays near zero in the twelve ban states, which hold ~34% of US children. ~55% of children live with a current user. ~7M live with a parent who regained after stopping, up from 6.1M because of the 2035 shortage and gray seizures.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL arithmetic. Medicare 19.6M users. Existing codes: 14.0M × ~$218 avg net × 12 ≈ $36.6B. CMMI Metabolic Access Model (Part D, from Jan 2036; BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with prediabetes, hypertension or knee OA; manufacturer-agreed net $245/month; $50 beneficiary copay): 5.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $16.5B. Medicare gross incretin spend ≈ $53.1B a year, up from ~$36.5B. Medicaid: 22 states plus DC opted into the model's Medicaid track at a ~$185 supplemental-rebated net, at regular federal match, with no enhanced FMAP. 7.5M × $185 × 12 ≈ $16.7B, ~63% federal ≈ $10.5B. Free provision: the HRSA FQHC programme supplies Novo in-kind oral semaglutide under the Dec 2035 settlement, valued at a ~$95 340B-equivalent: 0.75M × $95 × 12 ≈ $0.86B/yr against the $2.6B three-year in-kind commitment (~$0.87B/yr). NY, CA and IL county programmes: 0.25M × ~$160 × 12 ≈ $0.48B/yr from state general funds. Medicaid in the twelve ban states cannot pay for weight indications under age 12.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $3–25 a month domestically across 150+ brands. Since India's B2C export registration took effect in Jan 2035, delivered gray prices to US buyers have risen to ~$40–110. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials run $30–80 through research-peptide fronts and now fill much of the gap Indian parcels left. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China still supply ~70% of world volume. Lilly launched retatrutide 12 mg in the EU, UK and Japan in 2035, and a Chinese triple agonist was approved in China at ~30% weight loss.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The shock ran upward. In Jun 2035 Novo recalled Wegovy pill lots and the product went on the FDA shortage list until Apr 2036. TrumpRx raised the Wegovy pill starting dose $149 → $199 and maintenance $179 → $249, and did not cut them back after the shortage ended. Foundayo rose to $199–239 on demand, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound to $249–299, MariTide $219 → $239 and retatrutide $299 → $349, with Lilly citing allocation and 2035 tariffs on imported intermediates. Orals fell from ~50% to ~46% of users. Gray users fell to 13.6M (~4.5M on Chinese 'reta'), and street prices roughly tripled for Indian product. Employer weight coverage slipped to 28%: some firms moved retirees and Medicare-eligible workers toward the CMMI model. ~13% still cover only through monitored metabolic tracks (~7.6M enrollees inside the commercial 15.0M). Lifestyle spending accounts reimbursing calm, focus or Reset platform fees rose to ~24% of large employers. Licensed longevity plans now run through retail clinics (MinuteClinic, Quest-partnered sites), which meet the in-person rules of the seven states. Amycretin ($1,249 list) and bimagrumab ($1,150) remain prior-authorised commercial products.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. ages 6–11 from Nov 2035)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; on Medicare model formulary from 2036)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab; not an incretin)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; semaglutide injection approved Nov 2035; both with growth-monitoring language; barred for weight indication by statute in twelve states)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmed by 2035 trial, full approval 2036)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by adults without obesity (~12M licensed cash plus a large gray share), now a routine retail-clinic line item
calm/focus plans (~4.6M) sold openly as 'steadiness' using label language
compulsion 'Reset' plans for betting, shopping, porn and screens (~1.9M)
gray 'reta' microdosing in gym and longevity communities
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is realised through existing and foreign products, because envelope rules forbid a new US molecule. Retatrutide 12 mg (~28–29%) was approved in the EU, UK and Japan in 2035 and added to the Medicare model formulary in 2036, which made pen-delivered near-surgical loss a public-payer product. A Chinese-developed triple agonist was approved in China in Oct 2035 at ~30% mean loss at 72 weeks, and its sponsor filed a US NDA in Jun 2036, so US approval is no earlier than mid-2037. The pediatric driver is realised by Novo's Oct 2034 filing of semaglutide injection for ages 6–11 (STEP Young programme), approved Nov 2035 with growth, puberty and ARFID-screening language. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out Sep 2035 (HR ~0.87 in obesity plus CVD), and the indication moved to full approval in 2036. Lilly filed the non-CVD extension in Aug 2036, so no approval before 2037. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 read out Oct 2036 with a statistically significant but small effect, and a filing is undecided after the scandal. Longevity remains off-label, with no ageing indication. Implants remain in phase 2. No oral matches tirzepatide. Brand prices rose rather than drifting down in this window.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens. Shortage-forced switches from the Wegovy pill to injectables in 2035 caused a GI spike from re-titration errors.
Elevated with rapid loss. Absolute cases rose with retatrutide in the Medicare model population.

No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis. Litigation centres on EPI. The first EPI bellwether (2035) returned a plaintiffs' verdict of ~$38M, under appeal, and its discovery produced the anhedonia documents.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 at more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Expected absolute fractures rise as 5.6M older beneficiaries start under the model, many of them on retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; the Medicare model requires a baseline DXA or a functional assessment for retatrutide but does not cover bimagrumab.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the unsealed pooled Novo data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Sep 2035 class labelling: clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~8% of patients on weight-management doses vs ~3% on placebo or controls, and ~11% on retatrutide 12 mg. The label also gives a low-dose estimate (oral ≤7 mg or equivalent) of ~4% vs ~3%, with a wide interval. Estimates come from FDA reanalysis of pooled trials, including a 2031 Novo analysis that was not submitted, plus the 2033 observational study.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adverse-reaction and patient-information labelling with prevalence (Sep 2035). No boxed warning. PHQ-based anhedonia screening is recommended at 3 months.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. The 2035 shortage and gray seizures created a large natural experiment in involuntary stops, with regain fastest after retatrutide and gray 'reta'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Medicare model rules allow supply bridging during shortages.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D in low-intake users. Low ferritin in adolescent girls. Retail-clinic longevity plans now include the annual panel, but gray users rarely get it.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide. Tirzepatide's excess is still small and non-significant at 6 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; decades-long pediatric exposure; repeated cycling; people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~19M current users have a BMI under 30. The NIH normal-weight cohort enrolled ~40,000 but has no outcome data yet. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are poorly characterised.

FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~58,000. Indian parcel volume fell after Jan 2035 registration, and Chinese 'reta' share rose. State-lab 'reta' content still ranges 0–300%, with ~20% endotoxin-positive. Smaller counterfeit-insulin clusters recurred (~140 ED visits in 2035).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India export registration in force; import alerts extended. State felony laws now in 14 states. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak federally.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide prepubertal height-velocity deficit (~0.7 cm/yr) persists at 48 months with no catch-up. Semaglutide 6–11 trial data showed a similar-direction deficit (~0.5 cm/yr) that was not statistically significant. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide 6–11 approval carries growth, puberty and ARFID-screening language plus a 10-year height PMR. Georgia became the twelfth state to ban under-12 weight prescribing (2036).

safety_ledger.effect: Rebound craving and relapse after abrupt supply interruption (AUD, Reset and calm users)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Case series and EAP data from the 2035 Wegovy-pill shortage describe sharp returns of drinking, betting and 'flatness withdrawal' irritability within 2–6 weeks of involuntary stops. No controlled estimate exists.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA shortage communication advises bridging to an alternative incretin. No labelling.

food_and_beverage.state: About 52% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. The Medicare model pushed protein-and-fibre reformulation into senior-targeted lines (Ensure-style 'GLP companion' shakes are the fastest-growing SKU at Walgreens). Zip-code assortment planning is standard nationwide. Value multipacks shifted from Memphis-type zips toward the twelve ban states and the non-opt-in Medicaid South.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. The 2035 pill shortage produced a visible bump in Q3 2035 off-premise spirits sales in high-AUD-fill states, then faded. More brewery consolidation followed. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~6% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down, and checks are smaller. Senior early-bird menus at Cracker Barrel and Bob Evans cut portions after the Medicare model began. 'Tasting' portions are default in high-density zips.

apparel.state: Plus-size continues to shrink. Senior-focused retailers (Chico's, J.Jill) report size-run shifts downward. Resale serves cyclers and shortage regainers.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. SilverSneakers-type Medicare Advantage benefits added 'lean-mass' classes as plans sought to blunt fracture claims. Premium DXA coaching runs $250–450. Retail clinics bundle VO2 and body-composition scans with longevity prescriptions.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is 28%. Part D premiums rose again for 2036 as plans priced in model uptake, even though CMMI bears part of the risk. Adherence differentials persist. Lifestyle spending accounts reimburse calm and Reset fees at ~24% of large employers. Medigap and MA plans market model enrolment support.

pharma.state: Lilly gained on retatrutide in Medicare and price increases. Novo paid $4.1B ($1.5B cash, $2.6B in-kind supply), took a share-price hit after the March 2035 unsealing, and lost pill share during the shortage. Amgen's MariTide holds employer tracks. Chinese developers are now originators, not just copiers. Brand cash prices rose for the first time in a decade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is now the unmarked condition, and being off draws questions: a shortage, a seizure, pregnancy, a bad reaction, or principle. A lean older body at a Florida pool now often means a Medicare model card, not wealth. The upper tier signals biomarkers and lean mass. Regain reads as a supply story more than a willpower story.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the status object is the retail-clinic biomarker printout and a 'low-dose, screened' line. Medicare made retatrutide-grade loss ordinary among retirees in The Villages, Florida, which drained some prestige from thinness itself. In Memphis and the Delta the gray 'reta' wave thinned after Indian parcels dried up and prices tripled. FQHC free pills replaced some of it, at lower doses and with smaller losses.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short and protein-led. Church suppers in high-density zips serve tasting plates by default. The Bread Alone network claims ~900 congregations. Thanksgiving 2035 coverage centred on families split between on and off members, not on the drug itself.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the drug the way they once listed height, and 'not on anything' is now the line that invites questions. 'Biomarker verified' tiers persist. After the label, some profiles add 'screened for flatness' as a reassurance.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is mostly treated as a setting. People who stay off on principle, fat-acceptance revivalists, some MAHA families and Unmuted members, describe appetite as a faculty they are keeping. The pediatric approval turned children's appetite into the main moral battleground.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled since Sep 2035 at ~8% vs ~3% on weight doses, ~11% on retatrutide and ~4% vs ~3% at low doses. The low-dose figure rests on thin data, and the exposed population is ~12M longevity, ~4.6M calm/focus and ~1.9M Reset plan users plus gray microdosers. On the label figures, the ~8-point excess at weight doses implies roughly 3–4M Americans with drug-attributable anhedonia.
interior_life.framing: After the label, platforms not bound by the 2034 consent orders (Steady, Quiet Hours, and Reset brands launched by retail-clinic chains) quote it directly: 'fewer cravings, less pull'. The FDA treats this as communication consistent with labelling. The four bound platforms say 'balance'. Clinicians call it a labelled adverse effect. Unmuted says the side effect became the product.
interior_life.effect_on_work: B2B 'steadiness' packages are sold to call centres and logistics firms as attrition tools, reimbursed through LSAs. The Southern District of Ohio suit survived a motion to dismiss in 2036 on a regarded-as-disabled theory, and discovery is ongoing. Some HR departments quietly added the label's PHQ anhedonia screen to wellness check-ins, which lawyers warn could create medical-inquiry exposure.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~19% from 2032 in high-density states. Operators spent more on lobbying against Reset ads than on Reset-free marketing. 'Off for the album' became a music-press cliché after two touring acts paused their plans publicly. Slow games and ambient TV are mainstream.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples' therapists now run the label's screen at intake. The shortage produced a strange season of partners abruptly 'coming back', with arguments, desire and drinking all returning together. Calm-plan marriages remain stable and quiet.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Novo documents gave the restriction coalition its first federal hearing, a Senate HELP session in Oct 2035, but no bill. MAHA legislators turned the pediatric approval into the Georgia ban and campaign material. Seniors in the Medicare model have become a constituency defending a demonstration that has no statutory floor. Turnout evidence for a 'sedated electorate' is still absent.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on access, newly frank on risk. The FDA labelled anhedonia with prevalence, approved semaglutide for ages 6–11 and moved tirzepatide's dementia indication to full approval. The FTC–FDA consent orders still bind four platforms, and the FTC opened an inquiry into label-quoting 'steadiness' marketing without acting. Twelve states ban under-12 weight prescribing, seven require in-person visits for low-BMI adult prescriptions, and six ban social-media ads for off-label uses. Congress held hearings and passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: CMMI's Metabolic Access Model in Part D (Jan 2036) and its Medicaid track (22 states plus DC) make public programmes the largest payer. Free provision comes from Novo's settlement-funded in-kind supply through HRSA-supported FQHCs (0.75M patients) and from county programmes in New York, California and Illinois (0.25M), framed as counterfeit harm reduction. The model is a demonstration and can be ended administratively.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare model enrolment requires a 6-month weight or HbA1c check for continuation, so it is adherence-conditioned but not premium-linked. Employer vendor data flows are unchanged in law. LSA claims and PHQ screens add mood data to wellness files. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged. The Army oral pilot continues and was briefly disrupted by the 2035 shortage. DOT guidance is unchanged, so shortage-driven gray substitution among drivers went undisclosed.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C registration (Jan 2035) cut parcel flows and moved gray demand toward Chinese research-peptide fronts. The 2035 tariffs on imported pharmaceutical intermediates fed into brand prices. Novo's API recall exposed concentration risk in oral semaglutide, which needs large amounts of API. China now has its own approved triple agonist and a US filing pending.

events.event: Novo Nordisk recalls Wegovy pill lots after FDA inspectors find contamination at an API plant; the pill goes on the shortage list five months after India's parcel-export registration choked gray supply, and TrumpRx starting doses rise from $149 to $199

FDA adds anhedonia to all incretin labels with prevalence figures—about 8% versus 3% at weight-loss doses—drawing on a 2031 Novo analysis unsealed in March litigation; within weeks new telehealth brands quote the label in 'fewer cravings' ads
FDA approves Wegovy injections for children aged 6 to 11 with growth and eating-disorder screening language; Georgia becomes the twelfth state to ban weight-loss prescribing under 12 in March 2036

Novo agrees to a $4.1 billion settlement over the withheld mood analysis and undisclosed payments to calm-plan platforms, including $2.6 billion of free oral semaglutide for community health centres over three years
Medicare's Metabolic Access Model begins covering obesity drugs, including retatrutide 12 mg, for a $50 copay, and 22 state Medicaid programmes join; enrolment reaches 5.6 million by December
CVS MinuteClinic and Quest-partnered sites roll out in-person 'metabolic panel and microdose' visits in 40 states, and licensed longevity subscribers among adults without obesity pass 12 million

open_tensions: Public programmes are now the largest payer, but the Medicare model is a CMMI demonstration on top of a statutory exclusion. ~5.6M seniors, many on retatrutide with known fracture risk, depend on an arrangement a future HHS can end, and regain data say what happens if it does.

The label now says roughly one in twelve users at weight doses loses pleasure, and that sentence has become ad copy. The FTC orders bind only four platforms, the Ohio ADA suit is in discovery, and employers are buying 'steadiness' through wellness accounts while screening for its side effect.

A federal 6–11 semaglutide approval now faces twelve state bans. Children in ban states cannot get it, children elsewhere start earlier, and the prepubertal height deficit still has no catch-up data or final-height answer.

Brand prices rose for the first time in a decade while Indian parcels dried up. Gray demand moved to Chinese 'reta' vials with no reliable content, and a Chinese triple agonist with a pending US NDA could become either a licensed competitor or a larger counterfeit template.

prose.headline: The Label Says You'll Feel Less. Medicare Pays for It. A Third of America Takes It Anyway.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 nearly a third of American adults, about eighty-seven million people, take an incretin drug, and being on one no longer gets remarked on. The question people ask now is why someone isn't. Two years ago the growth came through cash and the mail. This time it came through the government.

In January the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services began a demonstration called the Metabolic Access Model. It lets Part D plans cover obesity drugs for a fifty-dollar copay at a price the manufacturers agreed to. By December 5.6 million seniors had enrolled, many of them on Lilly's 12 mg retatrutide, which takes off close to thirty percent of body weight from a weekly pen. Twenty-two states and the District brought their Medicaid programmes in. Counting the old heart, kidney and diabetes routes, public programmes now pay for about a third of all fills, more than any other payer. Congress never voted on any of it. The law excluding weight-loss drugs from Medicare is still on the books, and the model exists only as long as an agency keeps it.

Prices went the other way. In June 2035 Novo Nordisk recalled lots of its Wegovy pill after inspectors found contamination at an ingredient plant, and the pill was in shortage for ten months. Five months earlier India had begun requiring export registration for mail-order medicine, and the cheap parcels that had supplied millions of Americans thinned out. The TrumpRx starting price rose from $149 to $199 and stayed there after the shortage ended. Retatrutide went from $299 to $349. Gray-market use fell for the first time, and much of what was left moved to Chinese vials of uncertain content. People who were cut off regained. AUD and Reset users who stopped abruptly described cravings coming back within weeks.

The largest event of the period started in a courtroom. Discovery in the pancreatic-insufficiency litigation turned up a 2031 Novo analysis estimating how often the drugs dull pleasure, which had never been sent to regulators. The same documents showed payments routed through a contractor to two calm-plan platforms. In September 2035 the FDA put anhedonia on every incretin label with a number: about eight percent of people on weight-loss doses against three percent on placebo, eleven percent on retatrutide, and a thin, uncertain four percent at low doses. In December Novo settled for $4.1 billion. Most of it was free oral semaglutide for community health centres, which now give pills to three-quarters of a million uninsured patients. New York, California and Illinois run their own free county programmes and call them protection against counterfeits.

The label did not slow the calm market. It gave the market its wording. Platforms not bound by the 2034 consent orders quote the FDA directly: fewer cravings, less pull. Employers buy 'steadiness' packages through wellness accounts, and some have added the label's own anhedonia screen to check-ins, which worries their lawyers. The Ohio promotion lawsuit survived dismissal. Longevity use is now ordinary retail. MinuteClinic will do a blood panel and write a low-dose prescription in the same visit, and more than twelve million adults without obesity pay for such plans.

Children are where people argue. In November 2035 the FDA approved Wegovy injections for six-to-eleven-year-olds, with height and eating-disorder screening written into the label. Georgia became the twelfth state to ban it. In Florida's retirement towns the lean older body now usually means a Medicare card. In Memphis it may mean a free pill from a health centre, or a vial from Telegram. Spirits are down a fifth, sportsbooks complain, and supermarkets stock companion shakes beside the pharmacy counter. From the outside, nothing in the country looks broken.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Harlan takes her pill at 6:10 with four ounces of water, standing at the sink because the insert says wait thirty minutes, and she has never once waited sitting down. The pill is free. The bottle says CHRIST COMMUNITY HEALTH and, smaller, SUPPLIED UNDER SETTLEMENT.

At her first client's house in Whitehaven, Mr. Odom, eighty-one, shows her his Medicare card like a boarding pass. Retatrutide, fifty dollars. He has lost thirty-one pounds and complains that his belt has run out of holes. She tightens his compression socks and notes his weight in the agency tablet.

At lunch in the car she checks the Telegram group out of habit. Someone is selling reta again, eighty a vial, no batch number. She was on that for a year, down forty pounds, until a package got seized and she gained most of it back in five months. Her sister asked at Easter why she'd gone off, as though Denise had decided to.

At three, Malik's school calls. He's ten. The pediatrician said there's a shot now, approved in November, but not in Tennessee. Denise says okay to the nurse about the ice pack and hangs up.

At night her cousin Trina comes by with tasting plates from the church supper and her phone open to an ad: Steady. Less pull. The FDA says so. Trina's on it for her nerves.

"Do you feel less?" Denise asks.

Trina thinks about it longer than Denise expected. "I feel fine," she says, and eats one deviled egg, and leaves the other.
